sam patel: quick question — my kid has a hearing evaluation next Tue 10am, I'm in phased return (4hr). can i shift my hours that day or use intermittent leave?
michelle (People Ops): yes — two options: 1) swap your hours with your manager for that day, or 2) file intermittent family leave for a child medical/education appointment. we cover short appointments. :white_check_mark:
sam patel: great. do i need a doctor's note or paperwork? payroll cuts in two days.
jordan (Payroll): payroll coding matters. if it's under 4 hours, mark as "Intermittent FLA - child appt" or use PTO. if you take the full day mark as "Short day - parental leave". tagging benefits for verification rules.
lina (Benefits): for visits under 2 hours we don't require formal medical certs; add the appointment details on the intermittent leave form. if school requests employer verification we can provide a letter — ping me.
michelle (People Ops): please use the child-appointment form so we track accommodations. link: https://intranet.redwood/care/child-appointment-request
sam patel: if tara approves the swap, still file the form?
tara (Manager): yes file it for records and tag me. i'll confirm the swap in the schedule. :+1:
sam patel: FYI i'm on an H1-B visa — any special rules?
michelle (People Ops): same process for visa holders, just document dates. if travel outside the US is needed loop in Legal to check reentry and visa status.
jordan (Payroll): payroll won't change benefits eligibility but we need the coded reason for audit. please submit before payroll cutoff.
sam patel: thanks all — filing now and tagging tara.
